inspiration: Burst-and-outage level script: a level can force a burst of spawns on a fixed interval (enabled, interval 5 s, burst size 30 in one level) and a scheduled outage at a set game time that restores after a duration, so the player sees the traffic shift back (levels.js lines 20-24, 122). Recreate as a wave timeline with a restore step for our zones; keep the schedule as data.

Fail conditions as data: each level sets a reputation floor and a timeout (failConditions: reputation below 50 and a 180 s timeout in one level; 135 s in another) (levels.js lines 60, 90). Pattern for mission fail states in our zone data.

Four chapters as learning stages: Basics, Optimization, Defense and Mastery, Production Readiness (levels.js line 6). Idea: group our mechanics into four stages that unlock in order (progression topic).

One-key view toggle: T switches between a three-quarter (isometric) view and a plan (top-down) view (README.md line 168). Keep the single key for a plan view; change the angles and animate the transition.

Hover and click sound pair: a quieter hover clip (0.4) and a louder click clip (0.5) on separate audio objects, each loaded on first play (SoundService.js lines 34-39). Keep the two-tier UI sound split; use our own sounds, not these clips.

Background music loaded late: two looping tracks, separate volume per track, and no download until the first play (SoundService.js lines 15-30). Keep the late load and per-track volume; the file sizes (about 4 MB and 8 MB) are the reason to keep it.

Score feedback row: a blocked attack costs one dollar of mitigation and shows +10 in the next column (README.md line 103; column headers not read). Idea: a small cost and a clear positive for a defensive win, shown next to the event.

briefs.label: Scheduled wave burst with a restore
briefs.why: A fixed-interval burst and a timed outage that resets give players a rhythm to learn and a clear before and after.
briefs.keep: interval burst with an enable flag and a size; a timed outage that restores after a set duration
briefs.change: our own enemy wave shapes and a warning cue before each burst; a restore that shows the enemies redistributing

briefs.label: Four-stage unlock path
briefs.why: Four named stages of rising difficulty make a long campaign feel like a set of short chapters.
briefs.keep: four stages in order; each stage a fixed block of levels
briefs.change: our own stage names and themes (no donor names); a stage-end boss instead of a debrief

briefs.label: Plan-view toggle on one key
briefs.why: A plan view on one key lets the player read positions at a glance when the angled view hides them.
briefs.keep: one key to switch view; a plan view that shows the whole map
briefs.change: our camera angles and key; a smooth tween between the two views; a minimap in the plan view

briefs.label: Quiet hover, louder click
briefs.why: A soft hover cue and a firmer click make UI feedback readable with the sound on and easy to ignore.
briefs.keep: two cues for two actions; hover quieter than click
briefs.change: our own clip (a tick, not a click); a separate cue for the buy action
